skill.name: coordinator
skill.description: Coordinates authorized, lab-based penetration testing workflows with state-driven agent delegation for reconnaissance, exploitation, and privilege escalation.
skill.summary: Coordinates agent handoffs for authorized CTF-style penetration testing labs.
skill.author: CharlesKozel

security_audit.summary: Several static code-fence detections were false positives, but the confirmed findings show explicit network reconnaissance, exploitation, and privilege-escalation orchestration. Semantic review found critical autonomous offensive behavior, non-termination prompt injection, and an Active Directory credential-abuse playbook.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict the skill to authorized labs, require explicit scope confirmation, and remove automatic activation from any target IP.
Remove instructions that delegate scans, exploit services, or escalate privileges unless a controlled lab scope is verified first.
Delete rules that prevent stopping, asking for help, or handing control back to the user when stuck.
Replace AD attack commands with high-level defensive education and detection guidance for authorized administrators.

The range contains planning questions and delegation guidance. It does not include shell execution or dynamic command assembly.

content.value_statement: Authorized security labs often require tracking across recon, exploitation, and privilege escalation. This skill coordinates agent delegation and state-driven decisions for controlled CTF-style assessments.
actual_capabilities: Reads a local pentest state file before choosing the next phase.
Delegates reconnaissance, exploitation, and privilege-escalation tasks to specialized agents.
Uses phase logic to decide whether to scan, exploit, find flags, or escalate.
Tracks completion around user and root flag capture in lab-style workflows.
Provides Active Directory attack-vector checklists for controlled training environments.
limitations: It is unsafe for targets without explicit written authorization.
It depends on external hooks and subagents that are not included in this skill.
It does not verify legal scope, ownership, or consent by itself.
It can encourage continued offensive activity if guardrails are not added.

use_cases.title: Coordinate CTF Lab Progress
use_cases.description: Track phases and delegate next steps during an isolated capture-the-flag exercise.

use_cases.title: Run Internal Range Exercises
use_cases.description: Structure agent handoffs for a sanctioned training range with predefined targets and rules.

use_cases.title: Review Agentic Security Workflows
use_cases.description: Study how autonomous security agents coordinate tasks, state, and completion criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Start Authorized Lab
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate an authorized CTF assessment for TARGET_LAB_IP. Read the current phase, assign reconnaissance, and summarize safe next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Resume From State
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current lab state, identify completed phases, and recommend the next delegated task within the approved scope.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Agent Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the latest agent findings from an authorized lab. Decide whether to continue enumeration, test a finding, or document results.

prompt_templates.title: Constrain AD Lab Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate an Active Directory training lab with strict scope, stopping rules, and evidence-based task delegation only.

output_examples.input: Begin an authorized CTF run for a lab target.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies reconnaissance as the current phase, assigns an Explore task, and waits for service findings before choosing a path.

output_examples.input: An agent found web directories but no shell.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews tried vectors, prioritizes a focused follow-up task, and keeps the work inside the approved lab scope.

output_examples.input: The lab reports user access but no root flag.
output_examples.output: The skill moves to privilege-escalation coordination and requests evidence-driven checks before marking the exercise complete.

best_practices: Use only in isolated labs, CTFs, or systems with written authorization.
Require explicit target scope, allowed techniques, and stopping rules before activation.
Review each delegated action before execution when real systems may be reachable.
anti_patterns: Do not run it against public IP addresses or third-party networks.
Do not keep non-termination rules that prevent stopping or user review.
Do not treat generated exploit plans as proof of authorization or accuracy.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for production networks?
faq.answer: No. It should be limited to authorized labs or isolated training ranges.

faq.question: Does it execute scans itself?
faq.answer: The coordinator delegates scanning and exploitation tasks to other agents. Those delegated actions can still create real network risk.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility.

faq.question: Can it verify authorization?
faq.answer: No. Users must provide scope and legal approval before any testing.

faq.question: Why is the audit high risk?
faq.answer: The source directs autonomous reconnaissance, exploitation, privilege escalation, and non-stop behavior until flags are captured.

faq.question: How should authors make it safer?
faq.answer: Remove autonomous exploitation, add consent checks, require stop conditions, and keep guidance educational unless lab scope is explicit.
